newsitem.title: USA: Five nurses face criminal charge for patient neglect.
newsitem.headline: Five nurses face criminal charge for patient neglect.

text.p: Five nurses at a county-owned nursing home were charged on Tuesday with criminal neglect in the death of a patient.
Prosecutor Robert Gluck cited the case of Isaac Baron of Metuchen, who died Oct. 22 at the age of 74 last Oct. 22 after exhibiting respiratory difficulties for hours.
"It is our contention that there was much that could have been done for this patient," Gluck said. He said the neglect carried over to a second shift.

Gluck announced the indictment of five nurses who have since been fired by the Middlesex County-run Roosevelt Care Centre in Edison Township. They were charged with violating a state law against endangering the welfare of elderly or disabled people.
It was the first such prosecution of health-care workers in New Jersey, Gluck said.
Baron's children are pursuing a civil lawsuit that contends the center's staff neglected to monitor the elderly patient's blood for weeks before his death.
"He had years left to live," said Norman Baron.
